Both demo books show it: each seeds a converted pilot (Chipotle in the enterprise book, Rothy's in the SMB book) and the Dashboard still says 'Run a pilot whose result the buyer's boss could act on without you in the room.'
findings.current: readProofs() does `const arr = asArray(parseJson(storage.getItem("gtmos_poc_data")));` and loops over a top-level array. Pilot Desk saves the key as an object: `storage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify({ pocs: capped }))` (src/pilot-desk/lib/persistence.ts:132), and both demo seeds write `pocData:{pocs:[…]}` (js/demo-seed-data-ent.js:638, js/demo-seed-data-smb.js:449). asArray() of an object is [], so castProofs is always 0.
findings.problem: Functional defect, confirmed by running the aggregator (scratchpad script readiness-fable/run_poc.cjs): the shape Pilot Desk writes returns castProofs = 0; only a bare array, which nothing writes any more, is counted. Three results follow. (1) gateInheritable() requires castProofs >= 1, so no workspace can ever get past 'Partially documented', whatever is recorded; the Founding GTM state-change announcement that depends on reaching 'Usable with founder support' can never appear. (2) The blocker 'Run a pilot whose result the buyer's boss could act on without you in the room.' stays on screen after the user has done exactly that, and nothing the user does can clear it, so a first-time user is told something false about their own workspace. (3) The '…, but few pilot results are recorded' chip suffix and the 'Record results from 3+ pilots' item are permanent for the same reason. The 2026-11-05 label change to 'Pilots, reviews and handoff records' treated the symptom (the area read 'solid' with 'no pilot recorded'); the pilots were recorded and not read. Founding GTM's reader of the same key was already corrected for this (src/founding-gtm/lib/cross-room.ts:323-330, comment: 'reading the bare array off the real { pocs: [...] } object is what silently returned zero proofs before'). The unit test passes only because its fixture uses the bare-array shape with `outcome: "open"` and a `heat` object (src/dashboard/lib/readiness-aggregator.test.ts:191-202), neither of which Pilot Desk writes.

findings.problem: Every one of these strings talks about a pilot result, and the rule behind them does not look at results. readProofs() (src/dashboard/lib/readiness-aggregator.ts:217-240) counts a stored pilot when its outcome is any non-blank value other than "open". Pilot Desk stores the outcome as not_started, in_progress, converted or failed, default not_started (src/pilot-desk/lib/persistence.ts:55-60, 78-80), so once the storage read is repaired (previous finding) a pilot that has only been set up satisfies 'Run a pilot whose result the buyer's boss could act on' and is counted in '{n} pilot evidence records'. Executed (scratchpad readiness-fable/run_poc.cjs): a bare-array store holding one converted, one in-progress and one not-started pilot counts 3. The reverse also holds: the default Pilot Desk screen has no control for the outcome (only the two older screens do: src/pilot-desk/ds/components/ForgeForm.tsx:139, src/pilot-desk/components/ForgePanel.tsx:138), and the results summary it does collect is stored under `gtmos_pilot_desk_v1` (src/pilot-desk/v4/lib/pilot.ts:13, field `writeup`), which readiness does not read. So on the default screens a seller cannot record the thing these lines ask for. Two smaller points: with no pilot counted the chip says 'few pilot results are recorded' where 'none' is the fact; and chipFor() decides whether to add the suffix by comparing display text (`d.gaps.includes(PILOT_RESULTS_GAP)`, area-chip.ts:22), so rewording the gap line without updating the constant silently removes the suffix.

findings.proposed: Keep the counting rule and make the strings say what it checks, using Pilot Desk's own labels ('Define the pilot', 'Success criteria', 'Who approves the result', 'Save pilot setup'): verdict.ts:134, :177 and :68 "Define a pilot in Pilot Desk and save its setup: the success criteria, who approves the result, and when it ends." · dimensions.ts:280 "Save the setup for 3+ pilots in Pilot Desk" · dimensions.ts:293 "{n} pilots saved in Pilot Desk" · area-chip.ts:25 ", but fewer than 2 pilots are saved" (the suffix shows while 0 or 1 pilot is counted). Replace the text comparison in chipFor() with a flag set by scoreProof() (for example export `function pilotItemIncomplete(d: DimensionScore)` next to PILOT_RESULTS_GAP, or add `pilotsShort: boolean` to the score). To keep the result wording truthfully, count only pilots with a recorded result (outcome converted or failed, or a non-empty results summary from the default Pilot Desk screen) and give the default Pilot Desk screen a way to record the outcome. That changes which workspaces pass the gate.

findings.current: readDiscoveryStats() takes `advancedCalls` and `totalCalls` from `gtmos_discovery_stats` and the scorer (src/lib/readiness/dimensions.ts:178-202) presents them as "{n} discovery calls recorded with outcome 'advanced'" and "{n} Discovery Studio sessions" (gaps: "Record 6+ discovery calls with outcome 'advanced'", "Run 5+ Discovery Studio sessions"). The only code that writes that key is Cold Call Studio: incrementDiscoveryStats() adds 1 to totalCalls for every logged cold call and 1 to advancedCalls when the cold-call outcome is "meeting booked" (src/cold-call-studio/lib/persistence.ts:186-199). Discovery Studio never writes it; the result a seller records under 'How did the call end?' goes to `gtmos_discovery_call_log` (src/discovery-studio/lib/call-log.ts:236-285), which readCallPlanner() (line 166) counts as "{n} discovery calls prepared" (gap: "Prepare 8+ discovery calls in Discovery Studio").
findings.problem: All three Discovery lines name something other than what is counted, and two of the three actions cannot change the number. Executed with the engine (scratchpad script readiness-fable/run_disc.cjs): a workspace with 10 discovery calls run in Discovery Studio, each recorded as 'Advanced — dated next step set', and no cold calls scores 6 of 20, shows 'Discovery — limited', lists "10 discovery calls prepared" and still asks to "Record 6+ discovery calls with outcome 'advanced'" and "Run 5+ Discovery Studio sessions". A workspace that never opened Discovery Studio but logged 12 cold calls with 6 meetings booked scores 14, shows 'Discovery — solid', and lists "6 discovery calls recorded with outcome 'advanced'" and "12 Discovery Studio sessions". Because 'Usable with founder support' needs every area at 10 or more, a seller who does discovery only in Discovery Studio can never reach it, and nothing on screen says cold calls are what moves this area. Cold calls are also counted a second time under Outreach ("{n} cold calls logged"). The cause is the Call Planner retirement (owner decision, AUDIT_BRIEF.md section 4): Call Planner was the screen that recorded discovery outcomes into this key; the aggregator comment still calls the key a 'Cold Call + Discovery aggregate' (line 28).

OWNER DECISION: the better fix is to feed the Discovery area from Discovery Studio's own call log, which needs a decision about what the area should measure. One consistent option: 'discovery calls that advanced' = call-log records whose result is 'Advanced — dated next step set' or 'Won' (optionally plus cold-call meetings booked, as today); 'Discovery Studio sessions' = call-log records of any result; and drop the cold-call total from this area because Outreach already counts it. findings.problem: Semantic compression and high-context dependence. The approved change was that a blocker names the area and the action; in exactly the case where the seller has done part of the work, the line says only that 'more evidence' is needed, not which. 'run this' has no referent on the Dashboard masthead. The line-169 sentence puts an area name in front of a statement about 'at least one part of the sales process', so the reader cannot tell whether the named area is that part or why it was named; the same area can show the chip 'solid' in the panel (score 14 or 15) while it is listed as the thing to fix. The missing period makes these lines look different from the others in the same list. A second effect of the same cause: the named action is always the first listed gap, which can be the smallest item rather than what the area lacks. Executed (run_mine1.cjs case B): Deal management with 2 active deals, 2 next steps, 2 wins and no lost deals scores 7 and produces "Deal management: Record a loss reason on closed-lost deals." — an action a workspace with no lost deals cannot take and that is worth at most 4 of the 20 points.

Export from src/lib/readiness/dimensions.ts a `FULL_CREDIT: Record<DimensionId, string>` built from the saturation thresholds already in the scorers, and have dimensionBlocker() return `${label}: ${t("more recorded activity is needed.")} ${FULL_CREDIT[id]}` when there is no listed gap. Texts (numbers are the thresholds in scoreOutreach/scoreDiscovery/scoreDeals/scoreProof/scoreIcp): Outreach — "Full credit is 30 outbound messages, 15 cold calls, 12 LinkedIn actions and 12 different accounts." · Discovery — "Full credit is 8 discovery calls with a recorded result, 6 calls that led to a next meeting and 5 calls logged." (cannot occur today: an ICP area with no gap scores at least 17). For the 'one area at 16' rule (lines 161-174) say why the area is named: `t("One area has to be nearly complete. Engine output (run_cases.cjs cases 1, 2, 4; run_sweep.cjs): empty workspace → "Complete two readiness actions: Define your first ICP in ICP Studio; Record 30+ outbound touches"; after doing exactly those two things (one ICP at quality 30, 30 touches to 3 accounts; scores 8 and 7) the state is still Founder-dependent and the line becomes "Complete two readiness actions: Complete the missing ICP criteria; current quality is below 75/100; Log 15+ cold calls"; with Discovery already at 12 → "Complete two readiness actions: Prepare 8+ discovery calls in Discovery Studio; Record a next step on every active deal"; when one of the two areas has no listed gap → "Complete two readiness actions: Record results from 3+ pilots" (4,864 of 600,000 random inputs).
findings.problem: The sentence states a rule the code does not apply. The gate is 'two of the five areas score 8 or more of 20', not 'two actions done': (1) completing the two named actions can leave the state unchanged and the line then asks for two different actions; (2) it can list a single action after the words 'two readiness actions'; (3) it names an action for an area that already meets the threshold when only one more area is needed; (4) the ICP gap contains a semicolon, so with the semicolon separator one action reads as two ('Complete the missing ICP criteria; current quality is below 75/100; Log 15+ cold calls' looks like three items); (5) 'readiness actions' is a label the reader has not met, and the line has no end punctuation. For a first-time user this is the first instruction the Dashboard gives.

findings.problem: (1) 'Outbound touches' is not a term the default screens use for this record: Outbound Studio's button is 'Mark sent', its toast 'Logged as sent to …' and its list 'Outreach log' (src/outbound-studio/v4/OutboundStudioV4.tsx:217-220, 266), and the activity panel says 'messages & calls'.
